witnesses.Nippur: The Nippur tablet of the code (University Museum, Philadelphia, PBS V no. 93, reverse, Plate XL; a school copy, six columns of 58–60 lines, the laws separated by ruled lines), in Scheil's reading as published by Cuq 1918 pp. 8–10 (cols. I–II) and p. 87–88 (col. III); the signs are Poebel's autograph, Plate XL
witnesses.DT81: Kuyunjik tablet DT 81 col. IV (Assyrian copy), as in Kohler & Ungnad II pp. 36–37 — only a parallel text to the Nippur law 97

notation: Notation: Kohler–Ungnad 1909 / Cuq 1918 syllabic transliteration, q for their ḳ, plain š/ṣ/ṭ/ḫ. [ ] = broken or restored by the editor and NOT adopted as signs (the drafter reads the autograph/plate); (?) = the editor's doubt; ⟨ ⟩ = signs of that line taken from a different tablet than the line's witness (the Assyrian copy named in the unit's note), as Kohler–Ungnad print them in italics; ga = the GA sign read qa. Law numbers: Cuq's articles 90–97 and 98 (end only); Cuq's 'article 100' (the partnership law) is numbered 99 here and the opening of his 'article 101' (the agent law, whose last lines are the stele's §100–101) is numbered 100, so that no number is used twice with the stele.

units.ref: Nippur col. I lines 1–3 (the last words of a law before §90; about 30 lines above are broken away)
Nippur col. I lines 5–12 (loans at interest: the rate)
Nippur col. I lines 14–27 (the debtor with no silver pays in grain by the king's schedule; the creditor who demands more loses all)
Nippur col. I lines 29–35 (a creditor who has taken the interest … ; the end of the law, about five lines, is broken away)
Nippur col. I, five lines lost at the foot of the column (Cuq: 'Manquent 5 lignes')
Nippur col. II, about twenty lines lost at the head of the column — all of Cuq's article 93 and the beginning of article 94
Nippur col. II lines 1–8 (the end of the law: a creditor who has not entered the repayment or written a supplementary tablet, or who adds interest to capital, pays back double what he took)
Nippur col. II lines 10–21 (a creditor who gave with a small measure and took with a large one loses all; lines 13 and 17–18 are very doubtful)
Nippur col. II lines 23–28 (a loan made on a day when the control (NER) did not … loses all; Cuq notes that three clearly visible signs, ûm NER la, were left untranscribed by Scheil)

Nippur col. II lines 30–40 (the borrower with no silver or grain delivers his goods before witnesses and the creditor must accept; Cuq's line 36 reads ga-ti-šu = qa-ti-šu; the same law is on the Assyrian tablet DT 81 col. IV, which Ungnad numbers 'cca. 96' — see parallels)

parallels.ref: DT 81 col. IV = stele col. XXIII 1–20 (Assyrian copy; Kohler–Ungnad pp. 36–37 'cca. 96'; entirely italic, i.e. restored from this Assyrian text)

units.ref: Nippur col. III, about twenty-two lines lost at the head of the column (Cuq: two laws, his articles 98–99; only the last word survives)
Nippur col. III line 1 (the penalty at the end of a lost law: 'he shall be killed')
Nippur col. III lines 3–7 (partners: profit and loss are shared equally before the gods; Cuq's 'article 100')

Nippur col. III lines 9–19 (the merchant gives silver to his agent to trade; the agent goes on a journey; the opening of the law whose last lines are the stele's §100–101. Cuq restores lines 16–19 from the Louvre text, which this firing does not adopt as signs; lines 20–29 are on the stele and are not repeated here)

gaps: Nippur col. I: about 30 lines lost above line 1, and 5 lines lost after line 35.
Nippur col. II: about 20 lines lost at the top (Cuq's article 93 and the beginning of 94).
Nippur col. III: about 22 lines lost at the top (Cuq's articles 98–99).
Nippur col. III lines 20–29 are the stele's §100 and §101 and belong to the part laws-100-111.
Everything between Ungnad's §cca. 78 and the Nippur laws (the rest of the erased columns, ≈ §§ 79–89) is preserved by no edition in this repository: a gap.

Cuq's readings of the Nippur tablet are Scheil's of 1916; Poebel's Plate XL shows the signs. This firing transcribed Cuq's printed readings; the drafting firings must read the plate for every sign and flag differences. Doubtful readings: col. II 3 (uš-ta-aḫ-ri-šu), 13–18 (broken and conjectural), 36 (ga-ti-šu), 40 (u-pa-aṣ — DT 81 has up-pa-aš-ma).
